_about: Single source of the A2.5 hard-blocker regexes, read by scripts/prescreen_jd.py (and through it keyword_prefilter.py). Patterns are Python regexes matched against the lowercased JD. Categories and patterns are checked in order and the first match wins. Add a pattern only with `prescreen_jd.py add` (it validates the regex against the JD sentence and records the catch in candidate_context.md); never edit this file or the script by hand.

ITAR / US Person.note: Caught manually in A5: ASML J-00352651 "legally authorized to access such controlled technology" citing the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730)

US Citizenship / PR Required.note: Caught live: Niyam IT "US Citizenship with ability to successfully complete a federal background investigation." — bare noun-phrase bullet, no "requires"/"must be" verb.

No Sponsorship.note: Caught live: TP-Link "continuous work authorization in the US without the need for visa sponsorships"
Bare forms. candidate_context.md lists these and the regex layer must agree with it, or A2.5 passes a JD that A5 would then have to catch.
Caught live: Motorola "Employer work permit sponsorship is not available for this position"
Caught live: Caterpillar "Visa sponsorship is NOT provided for this position"
Caught live: Eaton "will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support... will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans"

Caught manually in A5: Vertiv (all US reqs on egup.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com), 2026-09-21 — "This is not a position for which sponsorship will be provided. Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F-1, H-1... are not eligible for hire."

Caught manually in A5: Grainger Businesses (Embedded Systems Engineer, req 335303), 2026-09-24 — "This position is not eligible for any form of sponsorship now or in the future. Individuals requiring sponsorship (e.g. OPT or H1B visa status) should not apply."

Caught manually in A5: Ford Motor Company (Embedded Software Engineer, Sunrise FL, hybrid), 2026-09-30 — "This position does not support sponsorship." Bare "does not support" phrasing; every prior pattern used offer/provide/available/eligible.

Caught manually in A5: Blue River Technology / John Deere (Software Engineer, See & Spray, Santa Clara CA), 2026-10-01 — "Visa sponsorship: Not available." Label-colon form, with the negation AFTER "sponsorship"; earlier patterns all put the negation first or used "is".

Caught manually in A5: IDEX / Advanced Flow Solutions (Software Engineer - Embedded Systems, Oklahoma City OK / Remote USA, R-10076), 2026-10-08 — "This role is not available for employment visa sponsorship." Subject is the ROLE, not sponsorship, so every prior "sponsorship is not available" pattern missed it.

Caught manually in A5: CRABI (Robotics GNC Engineer, Medford MA), 2026-10-05 — "The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa, now or in the future." Verb is "will not consider ... who require sponsorship".

Caught manually in A5: Optimove (Machine Learning Engineer, Dundee, Scotland), 2026-10-04 — "Must be eligible to work in the UK - we are unable to provide sponsorship at this time." Existing pattern only matched "not able to provide"; "unable to" slipped through.

Caught manually in A5: Bright Vision Technologies (Embedded AI Engineer, Remote US), 2026-10-08 — "We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position." Verb is bare "sponsor" + H-1B object, not the noun "sponsorship".
